service.name: Soul and R&B band
service.serviceType: Soul and R&B cover band for company holiday parties, galas, after-parties and wedding receptions
service.description: A soul and R&B band singing Stevie Wonder, Aretha Franklin, Al Green, Bill Withers, Marvin Gaye and the Motown songbook, a quartet or a five to six piece with a horn, for company holiday parties, galas, after-parties, milestone birthdays and wedding receptions across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What does the soul and R&B band play?
faqs.a: Stevie Wonder, Aretha Franklin, Al Green, Bill Withers, Marvin Gaye, Otis Redding, The Temptations and the Motown songbook, sung out front, with a horn on the big choruses. These are the songs a whole ballroom knows the words to across three generations, which is why this is the band for the floor after a program.

faqs.q: Which events book a soul band?
faqs.a: Office holiday parties, the second half of a gala once the last award is given, conference and company after-parties, milestone birthdays, and wedding receptions where the couple wants everyone up rather than a playlist. It's a dance floor act with a dinner set in it, so it can also carry a whole evening on its own.

The quartet is the smallest build: a singer, keys, bass and drums, in 14 by 10 feet on two dedicated 20-amp circuits with a 90-minute load-in. The five to six piece adds guitar and a horn, and that's the version that sounds most like the records and carries a ballroom past two hundred.

It's a dance floor act, and it runs at the level your venue allows. Before the floor opens the same band plays a dinner set at conversation volume, 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table. If your venue has a decibel limit, give us the number and we'll build the set under it.

faqs.q: Can it follow another act, or hand off to the DJ?
faqs.a: Yes. It's often the second half of a night that opened with a jazz duo or a solo pianist through drinks and dinner, on the same contract and the same sound system, and when the night runs past the band the DJ takes over the same way.
